gap: No result ChatGPT got states today's maker-store prices for the 1 kWh LFP class: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 at $499 (1,024 Wh, 1,000 W solar), EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic at $459 (1,024 Wh, 1,800 W) and EcoFlow DELTA 3 at $579. Anker's own store still lists ChatGPT's 'best all-around' C1000 Gen 2 at $699.99, which works out to $0.68/Wh against $0.49/Wh for the BLUETTI and $0.45/Wh for the DELTA 3 Classic.
standout_why: The two cited pages carry no prices. yourpowersetup.com/en-us/compare/power-stations has specs only and was checked 2026-08-26. greenmachineadventures.com shows no prices and calls the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 the value pick only 'if substantially cheaper' than Anker or EcoFlow, without saying whether it is. The uncited outagereadyhq camping page has a dated 23 Oct snapshot with the Elite 100 V2 at $499 and the C1000 Gen 2 at $699.99, so that part is not new. No result names the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic or the DELTA 3 at today's prices, and none gives price per Wh.
decides: This settles Green Machine's open condition. Today the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (a Dealectric product) costs $200 less than the Anker C1000 Gen 2 at the makers' own stores, with 1,000 W solar input against Anker's 600 W, for about 0.1 lb more weight (Anker 24.9 lb, BLUETTI says 'only 25 lbs'). So for solar camping, the Elite 100 V2 is a better buy than ChatGPT's Anker and EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus picks. The Anker's $549.99 B&H price, which ChatGPT showed, would narrow the gap to $51, but I did not verify it. The DELTA 3 Classic at $459 is the cheapest 1 kWh LFP unit at a maker store today, but I could not source its solar input or weight, so it can't yet be ranked.
